mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has risen consistently from -28.6% (t-2w) to -17.7% (t-0w), signaling workplace return. evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 10.9 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the last 28 days, or WORKPLACES reverses to below -20% in any of the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT station mobility remains severely depressed at -49.7% (t-0w), indicating public transport avoidance persists. This sustained transit collapse prevents the mobility cascade that normally converts commuters into retail customers, keeping RETAIL_REC suppressed below baseline over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT remains below -49% across all four weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility rises above -40% in any of the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 5 percentage points despite TRANSIT remaining below -45%.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has stabilized near -14% (t-0w) after declining from -8.1% (t-3w), indicating outdoor recreation demand is capped. When parks remain suppressed, consumers redirect discretionary spending to indoor retail venues. This substitution effect produces a net increase in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as the outdoor-activity ceiling persists.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains below -10% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS declined from -8.1% to -14.0% then stabilized
failure_condition: PARKS mobility rises above -5% in the next two weeks and RETAIL_REC does not increase, or RETAIL_REC falls below -15% despite parks remaining suppressed.

evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined 4.0 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility rises above 8% in any of the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not increase despite RESIDENTIAL continuing to decline.

Simultaneously, RETAIL_REC has improved from -18.0% to -13.9% over four weeks. This decoupling shows retail recovery is driven by discretionary activity, not essential goods. If GROCERY_PHARM remains flat while WORKPLACES continue rising, RETAIL_REC will accelerate upward over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains between -1% and +2% AND WORKPLACES rises above -18%
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM rises above +3% or falls below -1%, or RETAIL_REC does not exceed -10% in the next two weeks despite both conditions holding.

This improvement despite transit suppression indicates seasonal demand for outdoor retail and recreation is emerging. Over the next four weeks, seasonal uplift will compound this trend, driving RETAIL_REC further positive.

failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed -12% in any of the next four weeks, or PARKS mobility falls below -20% in more than two of the next four weeks.

failure_condition: TRANSIT rises above -40% in any of the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC exceeds -10% in more than two of the next four weeks despite both conditions holding.
